title: Scalable generation of 3D pancreatic islet organoids from human pluripotent stem cells in suspension bioreactors
protocol: Follow strict sterile protocol to avoid contamination during differentiation preparation.
Passage maintenance line as described in step 4: Clump Passaging hPSCs in 3D Culture.
Reseed the maintenance line, start a parallel line for later differentiation.
Seed cells at optimal density (e.g., 0.6 × 10^6 cells/mL in mTeSR1 + 1:1000 ROCK inhibitor for Hues8).
Take a sample for analysis of pluripotency by flow cytometry.
Perform a half-media change after 24 hours.
Remove bioreactor from incubator, clean the outer surface with 70% ethanol and place in BSC.
Wipe dry with a Kim wipe.
Wait 3–5 minutes until cell clusters have mostly settled.
Open the bioreactor cap and aspirate half the volume (15 mL for the 30 mL bioreactor or 150 mL for the 300 mL bioreactor).
Be careful not to aspirate any clusters.
Keep the aspiration tip as close to the surface of the media as possible during aspiration to minimize cell loss.
Return culture to full volume by replacing with either 15 mL or 150 mL fresh complete mTeSR1 medium (no ROCK inhibitor).
Replace and tighten cap.
Return bioreactor to the incubator.
Perform a full-media change after all cell clusters have settled, as described in step 11: Step-by-Step Media Change in Bioreactors.
Replace spent media with fresh complete mTeSR1.
Perform a full-media change to s1d1 media (S1 Medium + Activin A and CHIR99021).
Remove all spent media without aspirating clusters.
Wait 24 hours after the s1d1 media change.
Perform a full-media change to s1d2 media (S1 Medium + Activin A).
No media change on S1d3.
Add keratinocyte growth factor (KGF) on days 4 and 6 for primitive gut tube induction.
Use a P1000 pipette to spin the impeller and draw up a representative sample for QC.
Transfer 0.5 mL clusters into a 24-well plate to take bright field images.
Measure cluster size.
Use the collected sample for flow cytometry QC.
Perform a full-media change to s2d1 media (S2 Medium + KGF) as described in step 11: step-by-step media change in bioreactors.
Slowly lift the bioreactor to allow clusters to settle.
Aspirate suspended clusters after they take up to ∼7–9 min to settle at this stage due to flowering.
Perform a full-media change to s2d3 media (S2 Medium + KGF) as described in step 11: step-by-step media change in bioreactors.
Aspirate any few clusters suspended in the media after settling time to keep sunken cells from sticking to the bioreactor.
Collect QC for the completion of stage 2 (stage 2c): use a P1000 pipette to spin the impeller and draw up a representative sample.
Mix 0.35 mL of sample into a 24-well plate for bright field imaging.
Measure cluster size in the collected samples.
Perform a full-media change to s3d1 media as described in step-by-step media change protocol.
Aspirate suspended clusters after 7–9 minutes if necessary to prevent cell adherence.
Perform a full-media change to s3d2 media on day 8.
Monitor and ensure that the medium is clear once clusters settle.
Collect QC for the completion of stage 3 using a P1000 pipette to spin the impeller and draw up a representative sample.
Transfer 0.5 mL clusters into a 24-well plate to take bright field images.
Measure cluster size.
Use the clusters for flow cytometry QC.
Prepare an extra half volume of basal S3 media (no factors) on day 9 for wash.
Perform a full-media change as described in step 11: step-by-step media change in bioreactors, through step 2.
Add half culture volume of fresh basal S3 media (no factors) and gently swirl bioreactor to mix.
Wait 2–4 min for clusters to settle, then aspirate away basal S3 media.
Feed with s4d1 media (S3 Medium + KGF, Sant-1 RA, ROCK inhibitor, Activin A).
Collect QC: use a P1000 pipette to spin the impeller and draw up a representative sample.
Transfer 0.5 mL clusters into a 24-well plate to take bright field images.
Measure cluster size for QC sample collection.
Use the measured clusters for flow cytometry quality control.
Change full media to s5d1 media (BE5 Medium + Sant-1, Betacellulin, XXI, Alk5i, T3, RA).
Perform a full-media change to s5d3 media (BE5 Medium + Sant-1, Betacellulin, XXI, Alk5i, T3, RA) on day 16.
Perform a full-media change to s5d5 media (BE5 Medium + Betacellulin, XXI, Alk5i, T3, RA).
Note the difference in media composition between days 3 and 5.
Remove Sant1 after day 3.
Reduce retinoic acid concentration after day 3.
No media change on S5d6 (Day 19).
Perform a full-media change to s5d7 media (BE5 Medium + Betacellulin, XXI, Alk5i, T3, RA) on S5d7 (Day 20).
Collect QC sample on S6d1 (Day 21).
Spin the impeller with a P1000 pipette to draw up a representative sample.
Transfer 0.5 mL clusters into a 24-well plate for bright field imaging.
Measure cluster size.
Use clusters for flow cytometry quality control.
Perform a full-media change with S3 media as described in step 11: step-by-step media change in bioreactors for stage 6 day 1, 3, and 5 of the rest of Stage 6.
Collect QC samples weekly to track the level of Nkx6.1/c-peptide copositive cells.
Maintain 3D SC-islets cultured for several weeks in stage 6 with an even morphology.
Monitor the size increase due to larger endocrine buds in 3D SC-islets.
Cultivate 3D SC-islets for up to 4 weeks to observe progressive amplification of insulin secretion in response to high glucose levels.
Cultivate 3D SC-islets for up to 4 weeks to observe progressive amplification of glucagon secretion in response to high glucose levels.
Prepare 2.8 mM glucose buffer by diluting 1 M glucose in KREBS buffer at a ratio of 1:357.
Prepare 20 mM glucose buffer by diluting 1 M glucose in KREBS buffer at a ratio of 1:50.
Dilute 2 M KCl into LOW glucose buffer with a 0.75:50 dilution to prepare 30 mM KCl buffer.
Calculate the total volume of LOW glucose buffer needed as (5 mL * X) + (6 mL * 3 * X).
Calculate the total volume of HIGH glucose buffer needed as (2 mL * 3 * X).
Determine the total amount of KCl in LOW glucose buffer needed as (1 mL * 3 * X), where X is the sample number.
Place 12 inserts into the top two rows of a low-attachment 24-well plate.
Pre-fill wells containing inserts with 0.5 mL of LOW glucose Buffer.
Add about 250 μL of LOW glucose Buffer to each side of the insert.
Pre-fill the top 12 wells of 4 additional 24-well plates without inserts with 1 mL/well LOW glucose buffer.
Pre-fill another set of 24-well plates with 1 mL/well HIGH glucose buffer.
Pre-fill a third set of 24-well plates with 1 mL/well KCl buffer.
Pre-fill the last set of 24-well plates with TrypLE (1 mL/well).
Place pre-filled plates in a 37°C incubator to equilibrate for at least 15 min.
Collect 5 mL from each bioreactor.
Wash each sample with 2 mL of LOW glucose buffer in a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin down the samples at 200 g.
Resuspend the pellets in 2 mL of LOW glucose buffer.
Distribute the resuspended sample to the 24-well plate for hormone secretion assay and intracellular insulin content estimation.
Use 3 × 0.5 mL volume for assaying hormone secretion in triplicate.
Use the remaining 0.5 mL volume for intracellular insulin content estimation.
Distribute 0.5 mL from each sample into each of the 3 replicate inserts/sample (final volume per well is 1.0 mL).
Place the plate in the 37°C incubator for 1 h.
Process one plate at a time if more than one 24-well plate is used.
Aspirate LOW glucose buffer from the 0.5 mL leftover of each sample in the 15 mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL of M-Per mammalian protein extraction reagent to lyse cells.
Incubate samples at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for about 15 min.
Triturate clusters by pipetting up and down until all the cells are lysed.
Transfer 1 mL of insulin content sample into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Store the tube at −80°C until the time of the ELISA assay.
Remove the plate containing ‘glucose starved’ cell clusters from the incubator after 1 h of LOW glucose buffer incubation.
Transfer each insert into an empty well in the bottom two rows and let LOW buffer drain from insert into the well by wicking.
Pass inserts into the “LOW” plate and place it in the 37°C incubator for 1 h.
Remove the plate containing the inserts after 1 h of the last LOW glucose buffer incubation.
Transfer the plate to the HIGH glucose buffer prefilled plate for the HIGH glucose challenge step.
Repeat step 21dii of the LOW glucose challenge.
Transfer inserts into the HIGH glucose buffer containing plate.
Place the plate in the incubator for 1 h.
Remove the ‘wicked’ liquid from the 24-well plate.
Combine it with the liquid in the original well from which the insert was removed.
Mix using a P200 pipette.
Transfer 0.2 mL into a low-attachment 96-well plate.
Store at −20 to −70°C.
After 1 h of HIGH glucose buffer incubation, remove the plate containing the inserts as well as the KCl plate.
Repeat step 21dii of the LOW glucose challenge.
Transfer inserts into the KCl buffer containing plate.
Remove the plate containing the inserts after 1 h of KCl buffer incubation.
As well as the TrypLE prefilled plate.
Transfer inserts into the TrypLE containing plate.
Incubate the inserts in the 37°C incubator for 30 min.
Triturate clusters by pipetting up and down using a P1000 pipette after 30 min of TrypLE incubation.
Remove cells from the insert mesh without rupturing the mesh.
Transfer 0.5 ml of dispersed cells into a microcentrifuge tube.
Puncture through the mesh with a P1000 pipette and transfer remaining liquid into the same microcentrifuge tube.
Count the total number of cells in each microcentrifuge tube.
Dilute collected samples using x mL KREBS buffer for x number of cells.
Optimize sample dilution according to the number of cells assayed and their hormone content.
Use a 1:10 dilution for glucagon secretion assay in Hues 8 SC-islets.
Use a 1:50 dilution for insulin secretion assay in Hues 8 SC-islets.
Use a 1:5000 dilution for intracellular insulin content measurement in Hues 8 SC-islets.
Measure human insulin levels using ALPCO Diagnostics Insulin ELISA kit (catalog number 80-INSHUU-E01.1).
Measure human glucagon levels using Mercodia Glucagon ELISA kit (catalog number 10-1271-01).
Divide the measured hormone concentration by the total cell number in the sample.
Calculate the average from triplicate measurements.
Express secretion results per 1000 cells as uIU/mL for insulin or pmol/L for glucagon.
